findings.description: storage_encrypted = false disables encryption at rest for the RDS database, exposing all stored data including credentials and application data to anyone who gains raw disk access.
publicly_accessible = true exposes the MySQL database endpoint to the internet, allowing direct connection from any network and greatly expanding the attack surface.
The aws_instance.db_app user_data makes the RDS endpoint, username, and password publicly visible in the EC2 user-data and in the final published index.php, leaking the database credentials.

The ec2role is granted s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on all resources (*), violating least privilege and allowing the attached EC2 instance to perform any S3/EC2/RDS action including data exfiltration and destroying resources.
Egress rule allows all traffic to 0.0.0.0/0 (protocol -1, all ports), permitting outbound data exfiltration to any destination from the RDS security group.

The database password is stored in plaintext via var.password in user_data and the terraform state, and lifecycle.ignore_changes means the actual password is never audited by Terraform, weakening secret management.
